reviews.title: I want to love it
reviews.text:
It’s so close to passable it hurts, but it’s just such a buggy mess with bad UX that I can’t recommend it in good conscience to other people in my life.

Hard Mode is probably the app’s jankiest feature - it prevents you from editing settings and I have to routinely go through the accessibility hell of disabling it to fix app blocking that was broken by the last update. Also, requiring the user to draw a picture using their finger as a step to disable hard mode is simply unacceptable from an accessibility standpoint. I get that it’s a hard problem to solve, but the current “challenges” used to prevent you from turning off hard mode are truly awful UX. To date, I have had to turn off hard mode 4 times, all of them to make changes to settings to get the app to function the way it was previously functioning. Stop breaking the app and making me turn off hard mode to fix it.

Notifications don’t work - I’m signed into socialite itself and both Snapchat and Instagram through the app. Trying to enable notifications gives me a sign in button that, when pressed, leads me to a page where it shows I’m already signed in.

The connect apps screen is horribly unintuitive and brain damagingly stupid. You are able to pull the names of the apps I’m blocking to display them on screen - why do you need me to then select the app names from drop downs next to the app names? If I set SocialLite to block the Snapchat app, it should automatically associate that block with the socialite Snapchat app.

YouTube audio doesn’t work until you minimize and then re-maximize the video player.

Snapchat doesn’t work well ever.

This app is an incredibly convoluted mess that delivers the promised functionality about 2/3 of the time - the audacity to charge me $10 a month for this experience is absurd. The value you provide is removing features that other apps already provide - better UX for platforms people already pay for is not more valuable than the platforms themselves. A one time $29.99 license would be steep but reasonable. A monthly subscription is disgusting. 10$ a month is repugnant

reviews.title: Best Thing That Ever Happened To Me.
reviews.text:
I used to have the worst problem with YouTube.

As a kid I grew up watching YouTube videos. I loved them. I used YouTube for years. Although, once TikTok came around, everything changed. The introduction of their short form content style took social medias by storm and eventually, every social media platform started to use it. Everyone except YouTube.

For a while YouTube kept true to their identity as the long form content they built their app on…for a while. Then one day, they turned into everyone else with their introduction of YouTube Shorts. Now here I am, sucked into short form brain rot content right like everyone else except I have arguably the worst version compared to Instagram, TikTok, etc.

I tried to get away but it was a nightmare. Even stated using YouTube through a Google browser instead to thwart off my problems with the Shorts and attempt to just have my regular YouTube experience Still, no use. I couldn’t bring myself to not click on them.

When I discovered SocialLite one day after seeing a video of their ad, I was optimistic and gave it a chance.

Let me tell you, I’m SO grateful that I did. I now not only have kicked my problem with short form content, but I also have my old 2018 YouTube back! The nostalgia of my childhood came rushing back using the old platform I knew and loved! And not just that, I gained back so much time in my day by not being sucked to my phone anymore the way I had become since YouTube Shorts came around!

I pray SocialLite always manages to stick around because although it seems like a small thing or quick fix to some, to me, it’s changed my life. It’s helped me fix so many bad habits. I love YouTube, I’ll always love YouTube, but I also love my independence more than anything else. I was losing that by holding onto these memories of an old YouTube platform that was long gone nowadays. But now thanks to SocialLite, I’ve gotten back the things I’ve missed for years, and I couldn’t be happier.

Thank you!!!!! 10/10! Absolutely recommend to anyone and everyone!

reviews.title: Whoever made this app is a legend.
reviews.text:
Genuine review here.

Whoever made this did a great job. First of all the app selection is great, and the app works surprisingly well for a technically-web-based app. You wouldn’t even think it’s a website at times. 

They’ve gotten the app to work very well through regular updates, with this last one being a huge improvement. You can even watch YouTube with the app/phone closed, so listening to podcasts without leaving your screen on is possible. (Thank you). 

App blocks suggested posts and ads perfectly on all platforms. 

And all that before even mentioning how goated the app blocking is. It requires a lot of effort to unblock apps which really helps to stay off social media as much. You can even block uninstalling the app to bypass it. 

All I would ask as a recommendation is to make it just as difficult to disable sleep mode and the uninstall blocker. Bypassing sleep mode only takes one button press when it should be harder to evade. 

I’ve never felt compelled to make an app review before, but this one is just too good, the paid version is definitely worth it!

My only real issue I have with it is the bugs that happen very frequently. It seems that each app uses a custom browser-esque version of the app that can have some issues with playback or video quality, sometimes just not displaying the noise for videos.

reviews.title: No ads and no reels is worth it.
reviews.text:
as someone who was spending 4 hours on average a day on instagram, i am grateful for the removal of the curated desirability of the meta-made app. videos must be watched from start to finish at normal speed, no reposts, ad-free (timelines and stories) and reel feed-free scrolling creates a less dopamine heavy environment, which i am grateful for.

my only gripes in my few days of testing are the broken “copy link” button, when trying to share a link to an instagram post outside of Sociallite, and posting to stories feels clunky, and unpolished. i know the point is to reduce incentives to spend time on the app, but it feels like a feature that should either be similar to the original feel, or something that can be turned off. not sure what the image quality of a post will be like either, haven’t tried it yet. otherwise, great new app.
